root_cause: After a new Netlify_mcp DCR OAuth grant, Composio project-scoped connected accounts enumerated two ACTIVE accounts, although an earlier Platform tool log conclusively recorded upstream MCP StreamableHTTP HTTP401 Unauthorized for the old read-only get-project account. The prior Edge bridge unconditionally selected the first ACTIVE record without verifying Netlify-provider authorization and might keep using the stale grant. A later OIDC-only run 39234783733 confirmed two ACTIVE accounts and an unresolved read-only session execute HTTP400. Exact selected account was not logged; this selection defect is source-confirmed, but whether it alone explains the 400 is not yet proven.
intervention: Enumerate all ACTIVE/complete/undisabled netlify_mcp connections across bounded cursor pages, refuse >4 candidates, sort by creation time as a preference only, and perform a real site-ID-scoped provider get-project read on each candidate through the existing strict OIDC bridge. Bind any subsequent backup deploy proxy only to a candidate with proven read access. Health never executes deploy-site. If all candidates reject or mismatch site, fail with explicit 424 and do not create a deployment.
prevention: Never treat Composio ACTIVE as upstream Netlify OAuth proof. Each backup write must first pass a read-only provider check on the same exact connected account/site in that invocation; immutable OIDC, fixed tool allowlist, fixed site, no credentials or account identifiers in logs, bounded attempts, Required CI/CodeQL, protected merge, exact production readback.
